mainTopic: Selling a wife's כתובה to pay for injuries, כתובת בנין דכרין, and whether תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about a wife who injured someone: why can't she sell the 'benefit value' (טובת הנאה) of her כתובה in a way where her later מחילה causes no loss? The גמרא answers that she will surely forgive whatever benefits her husband, so בית דין does not bother arranging a useless sale. It then asks why a wife who injured her husband cannot sell her כתובה to him, and answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who forbids a husband to live with his wife without a כתובה. To make רבי מאיר's reason fit, the גמרא sets the case up first with a large כתובה, and then with a כתובה of only the Torah amount, where four זוזים of damages would not lead him to give up twenty-five. A later line of the ברייתא seems to contradict this. רבא explains that line as being about כתובת בנין דכרין, which a woman does not lose by selling her כתובה, because she sold only out of need for money. Finally, the גמרא asks whether תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים, based on two ברייתות about עבדי מלוג going free through שן ועין. It rejects this proof in two ways. The second way leans on a statement of רבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Her forgiving would cause no loss here
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: there is a way to sell where her later מחילה toward the husband would not make anyone lose, since even now she pays nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if she forgives her כתובה toward her husband, the person she injured does not lose anything, since right now too she is not giving him anything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that began just before this point. It argues that there is a case where her forgiving the כתובה would not cause anyone to lose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason for not letting her sell was that she might forgive the כתובה to her husband, leaving the buyer empty-handed. The challenger says that the injured person, as buyer, would lose nothing even if she forgives, because right now she is paying him nothing anyway. So the worry about מחילה should not block the sale.

phrases.english: For if she forgives toward the husband —
phrases.notes: This line ends a question that started before this point. She would be forgiving her כתובה debt.

phrases.english: he does not lose,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person she injured, who would get the sale. It is not her husband.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי לָא מִידֵּי קָא יָהֲבָה לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: since now too she is not giving him anything!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מָחֲלָה לְגַבֵּי בַעַל לָא קָא מַפְסֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge from the text before this section against the מחילה reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fear of מחילה prevents her from selling the טובת הנאה of her כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her forgiving causes no loss, the fear of מחילה is not a reason to block the sale.

steps.title: She will forgive anything for her husband, so the court does not bother
steps.stepSummary: In the end she will surely forgive whatever benefits her husband, and בית דין does not trouble itself for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, anything that benefits her husband she will certainly forgive. And we do not make בית דין go to trouble for no reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Since she will certainly forgive the כתובה for her husband's benefit, the sale would accomplish nothing, so בית דין does not arrange it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that this setup causes no loss. Its point is that the sale is useless: the forgiving is so certain that the sale will never actually bring anything in. A court does not supervise a pointless sale.

phrases.english: In the end,
anything toward the husband — she will certainly forgive,
and to trouble the court for nothing
we do not trouble.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical futility: the sale would never actually accomplish anything.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since nobody loses, the sale should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her מחילה toward her husband is certain, so the sale is useless and בית דין will not arrange it.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא about a wife who injured her husband
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a wife who injured her husband keeps her כתובה. Why not let her sell it to him? Her forgiving it to him would cause no loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא: 'Similarly, a wife who injured her husband has not lost her כתובה'? Why not? Let her sell her כתובה's benefit value to her husband for this injury. If she forgives it toward her husband, nobody loses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and challenges it. If the only problem with selling is her possible מחילה, that problem does not exist when the buyer is the husband himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband himself is the buyer, her forgiving the כתובה to him hurts no one, because he is the one who would hold it. So the reason from step 2 does not explain why the ברייתא lets her keep her כתובה untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: that which is taught in a ברייתא
marriage contract; the money owed to a wife upon divorce or widowhood
the small 'benefit value' of a right that may or may not be collected

phrases.english: But that which is taught in a ברייתא:
And similarly, she who injured her husband —
has not lost her כתובה,
why?
Let her sell her כתובה to her husband
for its benefit value —
for this injury,
for if she forgives toward the husband,
there is no loss!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מחילה reasoning of step 2 to challenge a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא ruling that a wife who injured her husband keeps her כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the husband is the buyer, the מחילה worry disappears, so she should be able to sell it to him to pay for his injury.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the husband is losing out by buying. The point is that if she forgives the כתובה to him, he loses nothing, because he is the one who owes it.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is רבי מאיר, who forbids a man to stay with his wife even one hour without a כתובה. Selling it to him would leave her without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is certainly רבי מאיר, who says: a man is forbidden to keep his wife even one hour without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. Selling the כתובה to her husband would leave her married without a כתובה, which he forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is no longer about her forgiving the debt. A different rule blocks the sale: a wife must always have a כתובה. If she sold it to her husband, she would be living with him without one.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא whose opinion the ברייתא is said to follow
that he keep or remain with

phrases.english: This is certainly רבי מאיר,
who says: it is forbidden for a man
to keep his wife
even one hour without a כתובה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a specific תנא whose rule blocks the sale.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She should be able to sell the כתובה to her husband, since no loss results.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר she may not be left without a כתובה, so she cannot sell it to her husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a sale can be blocked by a rule protecting the marriage, not only by worry about the buyer's loss.

steps.title: What is the reason for רבי מאיר's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lies behind רבי מאיר's rule that a wife must always have a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי מאיר's rule. This is setting up the next move, where it checks whether that reason fits our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the reason matters here. The גמרא wants to see whether the purpose of the rule actually applies when the husband buys the כתובה because she injured him.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the rule cited in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of רבי מאיר's ban on living with a wife without a כתובה.

steps.title: So divorcing her will not be easy, and here he would divorce and collect
steps.stepSummary: The rule exists so that divorcing her will not be easy for him. Here, if he bought her כתובה, he would divorce her and keep it as payment for his injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that she will not be light in his eyes to divorce. Here, he would divorce her and collect it from her for his injury.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: a כתובה makes divorce costly, so he will not send her away easily. Here, owning her כתובה would let him divorce her freely and keep it as his injury payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כתובה he must pay holds a husband back from divorce. If he bought it, that pressure would be gone, because he could divorce her without paying. So רבי מאיר's reason seems to fit this case.

keyTerms.meaning: to send her out; to divorce her

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַלָּה בְּעֵינָיו לְהוֹצִיאָהּ;
phrases.english: so that she will not be light in his eyes to divorce her;
here, he would divorce her,
and collect it for his injury from her.
phrases.notes: He would keep the כתובה money as the payment she owes him for hurting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַלָּה בְּעֵינָיו לְהוֹצִיאָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and applies the reason to our case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כתובה keeps divorce from being easy. If he owned it, he could divorce her and keep it for the injury.

steps.title: Even now he can divorce her and collect
steps.stepSummary: If so, even without a sale he can divorce her and collect from her כתובה for his injury, so blocking the sale changes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even now he can divorce her and collect from her for his injury!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation in step 6. Even if she does not sell, he can divorce her and then collect payment for his injury from her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once they divorce, he owes her the כתובה and she owes him for the injury, so he can take one against the other. Divorce is already just as easy for him without any sale. Forbidding the sale therefore does not protect her, and רבי מאיר's reason does not seem to explain the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: now too; even as things are

phrases.english: If so, now too —
he can divorce her,
and collect it for his injury from her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the application of רבי מאיר's reason in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר's reason blocks the sale of the כתובה to the husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Divorce is equally easy without a sale, since he can collect for the injury after divorcing her. Blocking the sale achieves nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: The answer that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר is now under pressure. His reason, keeping divorce from being easy, does not seem to apply, because the husband can divorce and collect for his injury whether or not she sells.

steps.title: Her כתובה is large, so he will not divorce her over a small injury
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a woman whose כתובה is large. The husband would not lose that big sum just to collect a small payment for his injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where her כתובה is large. Because of that small amount he is owed for his injury, he will not lose a lot of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. Divorcing her really would cost him, because her כתובה is worth much more than his injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that he could divorce her anyway and take his damages out of her כתובה. The answer is that the damages are small and the כתובה is big. Divorcing her would mean paying out far more than he collects, so the כתובה still holds him back. If she sold him the whole כתובה, that protection would disappear.

phrases.english: For example, where her כתובה is large,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added by the corrected wording, so read it as נְפִישָׁא.

phrases.english: so that because of that small amount
phrases.notes: The "small amount" is the payment she owes him for injuring him.

phrases.english: he will not lose a lot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a large כתובה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a sale, the כתובה gives him no reason to hold back, since he could divorce her and take his damages out of it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her כתובה is much bigger than his damages, so divorcing her would cost him money. The כתובה only keeps protecting her if she does not sell it to him.

steps.title: Then let her keep the Torah amount and sell him only the extra
steps.stepSummary: If her כתובה is bigger than the Torah-level כתובה, she could keep the Torah amount and sell him only the extra to pay for his injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if her כתובה is larger than a כתובה דאורייתא, let us leave her with a כתובה דאורייתא, and the rest she should sell to him to pay for his injury!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 8. It points out that a large כתובה can be split into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's concern is only that she always keeps a basic כתובה. If her כתובה is above the Torah-level amount, selling him just the extra would still leave her that basic כתובה. So why does the ברייתא say she cannot sell it to him at all?

keyTerms.meaning: the basic minimum כתובה amount, here treated as set by the Torah
let us set it at, establish it as

phrases.english: But if her כתובה is large,
larger than a כתובה of the Torah,
let us set her at a כתובה of the Torah,
and the rest let her sell to him for his injury!

steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a large כתובה from step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A large כתובה can be split. Selling him only the extra still leaves her a basic כתובה, so רבי מאיר's rule would not stop that sale.

steps.title: Her כתובה is only the Torah amount, and his injury is worth four זוזים
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where her כתובה is no bigger than the Torah amount. His injury is worth four זוזים, and he would not lose twenty-five to collect four.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where her כתובה is not larger than a כתובה דאורייתא. His injury is worth four זוזים, and for four זוזים he will not lose twenty-five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 9 by changing the case. Her כתובה is only the basic Torah amount, so there is no extra for her to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no extra, any sale would eat into her basic כתובה, and רבי מאיר forbids that. Even so, the כתובה still holds him back from divorce. Collecting four for his injury is not worth paying out the full twenty-five.

keyTerms.meaning: his injury, the damages for injuring him
twenty-five, the amount of a כתובה דאורייתא in this step

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that forbids her to sell her כתובה to her husband is about a woman whose כתובה is only the Torah amount. Selling would leave her with less than a basic כתובה, while the full כתובה still keeps him from divorcing her.

phrases.english: For example, where her כתובה is not larger
than a כתובה of the Torah;
and his injury was worth four זוזים,
so that because of four זוזים
he will not lose twenty-five.
phrases.notes: Twenty-five is the full basic כתובה he would have to pay if he divorced her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן דְּלָא נְפִישָׁא כְּתוּבְּתַהּ מִכְּתוּבָּה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by moving the case to a כתובה that is only the Torah amount.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case again (a new אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her כתובה is above the basic amount, so she could sell him the extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her כתובה is exactly the basic amount, so there is no extra to sell. It is still big compared with his damages, so it keeps him from divorcing her.

steps.title: The later part of the ברייתא says she never loses her כתובה while married
steps.stepSummary: The later part of the ברייתא says a married woman cannot sell or lose her כתובה. Yet by the גמרא's own reasoning, a woman whose כתובה is above the Torah amount should sometimes lose the extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what was taught: just as she may not sell her כתובה while she is married to him, so too she does not lose it while she is married to him? Yet there are times when you will find that she does lose it. What would the case be? Where her כתובה is larger than a כתובה דאורייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem from the next part of the same ברייתא. That part says flatly that a married woman never loses her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9 and 10 assumed that the extra above the Torah amount can be sold, because selling it still leaves her a basic כתובה. If so, a woman with a large כתובה could sometimes lose that extra, for example to pay damages while she is married. But the ברייתא says she never loses it while she is married, with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: under him, meaning married to him
what is the case? how would it look?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is using the later part of the same ברייתא to test its own reasoning about the extra above the Torah amount.

phrases.english: But that which was taught:
phrases.notes: This is the later part of the same ברייתא from step 3.

phrases.english: just as she may not sell while she is under him,
so too she does not lose while she is under him;
but sometimes you will find that she does lose,
and what is the case?
For example, where her כתובה is large,
larger than a כתובה of the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of steps 9 and 10, which allows the extra above the Torah amount to be sold.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the extra above a כתובה דאורייתא can be sold or lost while she is married
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the extra can be sold, then a woman with a large כתובה would sometimes lose part of it while married. That contradicts the ברייתא's flat rule that she never loses it while she is married.

steps.title: רבא: the end of the ברייתא is about the sons' inheritance clause
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the סיפא of the ברייתא is talking about כתובת בנין דכרין, not about losing the כתובה money itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The latter part of the ברייתא is about the כתובה clause that the male children inherit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the קשיא from step 11 by changing what the end of the ברייתא is about. He says it is talking about כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed that the סיפא meant a woman never loses her כתובה money. רבא says the סיפא is about something else: her sons' right to inherit the כתובה after she dies. That way the סיפא no longer clashes with the idea that she can sometimes lose the extra amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
We have arrived at (we are now dealing with)
The כתובה clause that her sons inherit her כתובה money if she dies before her husband

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the woman's own כתובה money with כתובת בנין דכרין. The second is a separate right that belongs to her future sons.

phrases.english: Rava said:
In the latter clause, we have arrived
at the marriage contract of male children.
phrases.notes: This is the clause in the כתובה saying her sons will inherit her כתובה money after she dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לִכְתוּבַּת בְּנִין דִּכְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by reinterpreting the subject of the סיפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the subject of the ברייתא's סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא means a married woman can never lose any of her כתובה money, which would clash with the גמרא's reasoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is about כתובת בנין דכרין, which is not lost through a sale.

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא: a sale does not cancel the sons' right
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the full reading. A woman who sells her כתובה, whether to others or to her husband, does not lose כתובת בנין דכרין, because she only sold it out of need for money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא teaches. A woman who sells her כתובה to others does not lose the sons' inheritance clause, because the need for money pushed her into it. In the same way, a woman who sells her כתובה to her husband does not lose that clause, for the same reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא spells out how to read the ברייתא according to his answer. He compares a sale to her husband with a sale to outsiders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling to outsiders does not cancel her sons' right, because she sold only because she needed cash. She did not mean to give up her sons' inheritance. רבא says the same is true when she sells to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches (introduces a rereading of a source)

steps.whatToRemember: A woman who sells her כתובה still keeps כתובת בנין דכרין for her sons, because she sold only out of need for money.

phrases.english: And this is what it teaches:
Just as a woman who sells her marriage contract to others
has not lost the marriage contract of male children,
what is the reason?
It is money that pressured her;
so too, one who sells her marriage contract to her husband
has not lost the marriage contract of male children,
What is the reason?
It is money that pressured her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the full wording of the ברייתא according to רבא's answer in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whether she sells to outsiders or to her husband, כתובת בנין דכרין stays in place because the sale was driven by need for money.

steps.title: Is תקנת אושא a מחלוקת תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים. It brings two ברייתות that argue about whether a wife's מלוג slaves go free through שן ועין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים? One ברייתא teaches: מלוג slaves go free through a tooth or an eye if the woman knocked it out, but not if the man did. Another ברייתא teaches: neither through the man nor through the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to תקנת אושא and opens a new question. It brings two ברייתות that disagree, and this sets up its suggestion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave goes free if his owner knocks out his tooth or blinds his eye. מלוג slaves belong to the wife, but the husband eats their produce. One ברייתא says that if she injures them they go free. The other says they never go free, whether he injures them or she does.

keyTerms.meaning: The ruling made at אושא: if a wife sold her מלוג property during the marriage, the husband can take it back from the buyer
It is a dispute between תנאים
Slaves from the wife's property, where she owns them and the husband gets the use and produce
Tooth and eye: a slave goes free if his owner knocks out his tooth or blinds his eye

phrases.english: Shall we say that the ordinance of Usha
phrases.notes: This is the ruling discussed earlier: a wife cannot really sell her מלוג property, because the husband can take it back.

phrases.english: is a dispute of Tannaim?
For one baraita teaches:
Slaves of usufruct property
go free through a tooth or an eye by the woman,
phrases.notes: In other words, if the wife knocks out the slave's tooth or blinds his eye, he goes free.

phrases.english: but not by the man.
And another baraita teaches:
Neither by the man nor by the woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כתובה discussion and returns to the earlier topic of תקנת אושא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is תקנת אושא actually a מחלוקת between תנאים, shown by the two ברייתות about עבדי מלוג?

steps.title: Linking the slave dispute to תקנת אושא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes both sides agree that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף. It then suggests that they argue about תקנת אושא: the side that says the wife frees the slave does not hold of it, and the side that says no one frees him does.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that everyone agrees that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself. So is this not what they disagree about? The one who says the woman frees the slave does not accept תקנת אושא. The one who says neither the man nor the woman frees him does accept תקנת אושא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two ברייתות could depend on תקנת אושא. This completes the suggestion it opened in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the husband is not the owner, since owning the produce is not full ownership. So the only question is whether the wife counts as a full owner. Without תקנת אושא she can sell, so she is a full owner and frees the slave. With תקנת אושא she cannot sell, so she is not a full owner and the slave does not go free.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed (the גמרא's first assumption, which may be rejected later)
Ownership of the produce or use of an item
Is it not? (introduces a suggested explanation)

steps.confusionAlert: The word סברוה is a warning sign that the גמרא is only assuming this for now. In steps 16 and 17 it pushes back on the conclusion drawn here, that the ברייתות argue about תקנת אושא. It does not push back on the idea that owning the produce is not full ownership.

phrases.english: They assumed that everyone holds
that ownership of the produce
is not like ownership of the item itself;
What, is it not in this that they disagree:
that the one who says by the woman
does not hold of the ordinance of Usha,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא לָאִישׁ וְלֹא לָאִשָּׁה –
phrases.english: and the one who says neither by the man nor by the woman
does hold of the ordinance of Usha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the suggestion in step 14 that the two ברייתות argue about תקנת אושא.
steps.raayaObject: That תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two ברייתות about עבדי מלוג going free through שן ועין, read with the assumption that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף

steps.title: Both ברייתות hold of תקנת אושא but speak of different time periods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתות argue about תקנת אושא. Everyone agrees with the תקנה. One ברייתא describes the law before the תקנה was made, and the other describes the law after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds of תקנת אושא. Rather, one ברייתא is talking about the time before the תקנה, and the other is talking about the time after the תקנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from the last step. It says the two ברייתות are not arguing at all. They are just describing two different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the תקנה, a wife's sale of her מלוג property was valid, so she counted as the real owner and her blow frees the slave. After the תקנה, her sale is not valid, so she no longer counts as the owner and the slave does not go free. That means there is no proof that תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there; each source is talking about a different case

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות are not arguing here. They agree on the law and just describe different periods in history.

phrases.english: No; everyone
holds of the ordinance of Usha;
rather, here it is before the ordinance,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says the wife frees the slave. Before אושא, her sale of מלוג property worked, so she counted as the owner.

phrases.english: there it is after the ordinance.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ תַּקָּנַת אוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 15's claim that the ברייתות argue about תקנת אושא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two ברייתות can be read as talking about different time periods, before and after the תקנה, so they do not have to disagree about it

steps.title: Both ברייתות are after the תקנה, and the wife's side has another reason
steps.stepSummary: A second way to reject the proof: both ברייתות are talking about after the תקנה and both hold of it. The side that says the wife frees the slave has a different reason, which comes from a statement of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: both ברייתות are talking about after the תקנה, and both hold of תקנת אושא. Then what is the reason of the one who says the slave goes free when the woman strikes him but not when the man does? It is like רבא, because רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer for why the ברייתות do not have to argue about תקנת אושא. It is setting up its next move: it is about to quote רבא's statement, which explains the reason of the side that says the wife frees the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the גמרא does not split the ברייתות by time period. It says both hold of the תקנה even after it was made. The ruling that the wife frees the slave must then come from some other reason, and that reason is רבא's statement, which is quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; introduces another possible answer
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this one and that one are after the ordinance,
and they hold of the ordinance of Usha;
rather, according to the one who says
to the woman and not to the man,
phrases.notes: He means the slave goes free if the wife knocks out his tooth or eye, but not if the husband does.

phrases.english: what is the reason?
It is like רבא, for רבא said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different rejection of Step 15, in place of the time-period answer of Step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that תקנת אושא is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling that the wife frees the slave can come from a separate reason (רבא's statement), even if both sides hold of תקנת אושא
